messages:
alex: Heads up — ap-southeast GPU pool is saturated, queue depth for model redwood/mosaic-4b jumped to 4200 across shards, p95 token latency up from 220ms -> 1.6s, and we’re seeing ~=2% request drops. Can we triage? :eyes:

infra-bot: Alert: ap-southeast1 GPU pool utilization 98%. QueueDepth(mosaic-4b)=4200, DropRate=2.1%, BackpressureLevel=HIGH. See dashboard: https://rbwd/ops/dashboards/ap-southeast1

maria: Thanks. Is this traffic organic or burst from a customer test? Any big recent rollouts?

alex: No large rollouts in the last hour, looks evenly spread across keys. Spike started ~2129987600. Non-committed traffic is ~65% of requests to that model right now.

sung: Can we steer some requests to mosaic-4b-q4 (quantized) as a cheap fast-path? Quality delta reported small for many workloads. Also consider tightening admission for non-reserved customers.

ben: Agreed on steering. Also, cheap short-term: bump preemption on low-priority pods to evict <12h pods and free 4 nodes. That should recover ~8-10% capacity quickly. Longer term we need to look at committed vs burst ratio.

tina_oncall: I can run a quick steering job and enable the admission rule for non-committed. Proposed plan: 1) Enable steering to q4 for non-reserved traffic 2) Apply soft admission throttle (50% of baseline) for non-committed 3) Evict low-priority pods if still >95% util after 3m.

alex: OK run it. Please paste commands here.

tina_oncall: Running now. Commands: ```
# steer 20% of mosaic-4b non-committed traffic to q4
rbctl route modify --region ap-southeast1 --model mosaic-4b --variant mosaic-4b-q4 --percent 20 --filter "customer_tier!=reserved" 

# soften admission for non-committed
rbctl admission update --region ap-southeast1 --model mosaic-4b --filter "customer_tier!=reserved" --qps 0.5x

# trigger low-priority pod eviction (if needed)
rbctl infra evict --region ap-southeast1 --selector "pod_age<12h && priority=low" --max-nodes 5
```

infra-bot: Action acknowledged. Steering job started. Eviction job queued.

maria: Quick check — what's the estimated token-cost delta if we route 20% to q4? We need to track billing impact.

sung: Rough calc: q4 reduces GPU cycles ~30%, so cost per-token drops ~25%. With 20% steering that gives ~5% overall cost reduction for this model's traffic. Worth it for stability.

ben: Also open question: do we want to cross-region spillover to us-west2 for excess? Latency will increase but could be lower cost and prevent drops. Need to check compliance/customer constraints.

tina_oncall: Eviction completed, freed 3 nodes (~6% capacity), steering to q4 at 20% in effect. Admission throttle applied. Current queue depth dropping: 4200 -> 3100 in 120s. p95 down to 980ms.

alex: Nice. Keep an eye on drop rate. If drops persist >1% after 10m we either bump steering to 40% or enable spillover to us-west2.

maria: I’ll notify solutions to expect possible quality regressions for some customers and advise on targeted pinning to reserved nodes if they need high fidelity.

sung: Action item: run an eval diff for top-5 customer prompts between baseline and q4 variant and post results here. I’ll own that.

ben: Ops note — open a follow-up ticket to model long-term capacity needs in ap-southeast (proj +30% over next quarter) and to propose reserved pool expansions or committed discounts.

alex: Thanks team. Current plan: monitor 15m window, increase steering or spillover if needed, create capacity ticket. :rocket: 

infra-bot: Update: 5m summary: QueueDepth=2100, DropRate=0.8%, GPUUtil=92%. Next health check scheduled at 2129989400.
